questions.topic: Comparing a pure fifth with an equal-tempered fifth

stimulus.body: The working note below records the evidence for a claim about comparing a pure fifth with an equal-tempered fifth. equal temperament sets the fifth at 700 cents. A marginal reminder adds: exactly 700 cents. A reader must decide which of the four proposed statements the note warrants, without using outside knowledge.

questions.stem: The question turns on what the note above shows about comparing a pure fifth with an equal-tempered fifth. Given the proposal "Exactly 700 cents", which choice is consistent with the evidence in the passage?

answer.exemplar: An equal-tempered perfect fifth measures exactly 700 cents, seven equal semitones, 2 cents narrower than the pure fifth.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: equal temperament sets the fifth at 700 cents. On that basis "An equal-tempered perfect fifth measures exactly 700 cents, seven equal semitones, 2 cents…" is the supported choice.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: A courtly genre and its subject

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: Courtly love is idealized devotion to an unattainable lady, not physical desire, marital duty, or religious devotion. A marginal reminder adds: idealized devotion, unattainable lady. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: A reviewer is weighing competing claims about a courtly genre and its subject, among them "Courtly love is marital duty within a household". Based only on the excerpt above, which answer is the one the evidence warrants?

options.text: Courtly love is physical desire between social equals.
Courtly love is marital duty within a household.
Courtly love is idealized devotion to an unattainable lady.
Courtly love is religious devotion to the Virgin Mary.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: courtly love is idealized devotion to an unattainable lady, not physical desire, marital duty, or religious devotion. On that basis "Courtly love is idealized devotion to an unattainable lady" is the supported choice. Option A ("Courtly love is physical desire between social equals") fails because it reduces it to physical desire; Option B ("Courtly love is marital duty within a household") fails because it confuses with marriage; Option D ("Courtly love is religious devotion to the Virgin Mary") fails because it confuses with Marian devotion.
